salve1.definition: salvē adv. salvus, well, in good health, in good condition .—Only in the colloq. phrase, satin' salve? (sc. res se habent?), is all well? all right? T., L.; see salvus.

satis1.definition: satis adj. (for comp. see satius), n indecl. 2 SA-.—Only nom. and acc, enough, sufficient, satisfactory, ample, adequate : cui satis una Farris libra foret, H.: Duo talenta pro re nostrā ego esse decrevi satis, T.: si…

scitus1.definition: scītus adj. P. of scisco.—Of things, fit, suitable, proper, judicious, sensible, witty : scito illa quidem (scripsit) sermone: scitum est, quod dicere solebat, etc., it is a witty saying : scitum est causam conferre i…

scitus2.definition: scītus ūs, m scisco, a decreeing, order, ordinance : plebi scitu, C., L.

scriptus2.definition: scrīptus ūs, m scribo, the office of a scribe, a clerkship, secretaryship : scriptum facere, to act as secretary , L.

se-1.definition: sē- in composition for sēmi, as in selibra.

se-2.definition: sē- in composition for sex, as in semestris.

se1.definition: sē acc. and abl. of sui.

se2.definition: sē or sēd praep. with abl. abl. of sui, by itself from, without, apart from : se fraude esto, XII Tabb . ap. C.—Esp., in composition, as in secedo, securus, seditio, sobrius, socors, solvo, sudus.

semi-.definition: sēmi- praep. cf. semis.—Only in composition, half-, demi-, semi- .

serum1.definition: serum ī, n 1 SAL-, the watery part of curdled milk, whey , V., O.

serum2.definition: sērum adv. neut. of serus, late at night : Quae Nocte sedens serum canit, V.

si2.definition: sī quandō (sīquandō) adv., if ever, if at any time; see quando.

si3.definition: sī quidem or siquidem (old sīquidem), conj, if only, if indeed: actumst, siquidem haec vera praedicat, T.: O morem praeclarum, si quidem teneremus!: siquidem . . . si minus, O.— Since indeed, since, inasmuch as: Siqui…

si4.definition: sī quī see 1 qui, 2 qui, and si.

si5.definition: sī quis (sīquis) see 2 quis and si.

sis2.definition: sīs for si vis; see 1 volo.

situs1.definition: situs adj. P. of sino, placed, set, lying, situate : Romuli lituus, cum situs esset in curiā Saliorum, etc.: in ore sita lingua est: in ipsis penetralibus (Britanniae), Ta.—Of places, lying, situate : locus in mediā i…

situs2.definition: situs ūs, m 1 SA-, a situation, position, site, location, station : cuius hic situs esse dicitur: urbs situ nobilis: locorum, Cu.: urbes naturali situ inexpugnabiles, L.: Africae, S.: castrorum, Cs.: turris situ edita…

solum1.definition: solum ī, n the lowest part, bottom, ground, base, foundation, floor, pavement, site: sola marmorea: (templi) Marmoreum, O.: ut eius (fossae) solum pateret, Cs.: (amnis) puro solo excipitur, bed, Cu.—The ground, earth,…

solum2.definition: sōlum adv. 1 solus, alone, only, merely, barely (never with numerals, except unus): de re unā solum dissident . . . unane est solum dissensio?: si dixisset haec solum, omni supplicio est dignus: hominum solum auribus …

sortitus2.definition: (sortītus, ūs) m sortior, a casting of lots, drawing : consul sortitu ad bellum profectus: quae sortitūs non pertulit ullos, i. e. for whom no lots were cast , V.

suasus2.definition: suāsus ūs, m an advising, persuading: ob meum suasum, T.

suggestus2.definition: (suggestus, ūs) m sub+GES-, a raised place, artificial height, platform, stage, tribune : suggestum in foro exstructum, L.: hac re pro suggestu pronuntiatā, Cs.

super1.definition: super adv. cf. u(pe/r, above, on top, over, upwards : eo super tigna bipedalia iniciunt, Cs.: Inplenturque super puppes, i. e. by rain , V.: superque inmane barathrum Cernatur, from above , V.—In number or quantity, o…

super2.definition: super praep. with acc. and abl. 1 super. I. With abl., of place, over, above, upon, on : lateres, qui super musculo struantur, Cs.: ensis cui super Cervice pendet, H.: super Pindo, H.: requiescere Fronde super viridi,…

supera2.definition: superā adv. abl f. of superus; sc. parte, above : subter superāque revolvens Sese, C. poë t.

suspectus1.definition: suspectus adj. with comp. P. of 1 suspicio, subject to suspicion, mistrusted, suspected : suspectum cupiditatis imperii consulem habere, L.: sceleris, Cu.: Non clam me est, tibi esse suspectum, T.: de novercā: ut regi…

suspectus2.definition: suspectus ūs, m 1 suspicio, a looking up, gazing upwards : Quantus ad aetherium caeli suspectus Olympum, i. e. height , V.: Turris vasto suspectu, V.—Fig., high regard, esteem, respect : honorum, O.
